philipp.goal: K-idol taper · fat loss · muscle retention

shared.goal: same exercises, own load — alternating sets

locationNotes.gym: Holmes Place · cable tower + machines. All primary exercises run on the cable tower — constant tension, exact progression.
locationNotes.home: Bodylastics tubes + door anchor. Bands mimic the cable tower 1:1. More resistance = bundle another tube. Height = anchor high/mid/low. Constant tension = stand farther from the door.
locationNotes.travel: Tubes only + door anchor. Everything with Bodylastics + door anchor, no dumbbells needed. Tempo 3-0-1 and standing farther from anchor substitute for more weight.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Fresh first — the most important move for the look. Constant tension at the bottom, where a dumbbell would give you none. Arm slightly bent, lead with the elbow to shoulder height. Goal: a clean 15, then 6 kg.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press (high-to-low)
exercises.cue: Anchor high, stand away from the tower, press forward and downward in front of the chest. The downward angle hits the upper chest automatically — the athletic line under the collarbone. 4 sets, because chest is your second focus.

exercises.name: Wide Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Second most important taper muscle after the side delt — which is why it is in both sessions. Pull the bar to the upper chest, feel the lats, controlled on the way back.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.cue: Was completely buried in the old plan — now a fixture. Elbows fixed at your sides, pull the rope apart at the bottom, brief hold. A defined arm, not mass.

exercises.name: Leg Press (light)
exercises.cue: Maintenance — hold, don't build. High reps, light weight, never progress. Keeps the legs lean and defined without making them thicker.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.cue: Fold the ribs towards the hips like a jackknife, hands fixed at the ears. Slow on the way back — that is the eccentric load.

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
exercises.cue: Lower back flat on the floor, arms long. Builds the deep abdominal tension that visually tightens the waist.

pull.title: Pull + Posture
pull.focus: side delt · lat · back · rear delt

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Second side-delt hit of the week. Exactly like Tuesday — constant tension, lead with the elbow. Six side-delt sets a week is the core of the taper.

exercises.name: Wide Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Second lat hit of the week. Replaces the pull-up you cut — that would have thickened the upper traps and shortened the neckline. The pulldown builds width without that drawback.

exercises.name: Cable Row (neutral)
exercises.cue: Sit upright, handle to the belly, elbows close to the body, shoulder blades together. Builds posture without thickening the neck — stay moderate, don't heave.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Cable)
exercises.cue: Gives the shoulder depth and the 3D look without mass. Arms almost straight, lead with the little fingers, squeeze the rear delts together.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.cue: Maintenance — the counterpart to all the pressing. External rotation keeps the shoulder healthy. Elbows high and wide, hands finish beside the ears.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Curl
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Holds the back of the leg — important for posture and for how trousers sit. Controlled, no swing.

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Elbows fixed, constant tension, brief squeeze at the top. Covers what the pulldown and row don't fully reach.

solo.title: Lower + Push
solo.focus: fixed machines only — no setup, no cable
solo.note: Monday alone in the gym. Deliberately machines only: fixed path, nothing can go wrong, no spotting needed. Cable exercises happen Friday with Philipp.

exercises.name: Glute Drive Machine
exercises.cue: Fresh first — your top exercise. Full hip extension, 1s hold at the top, squeeze hard. 4 sets, because glutes are the goal. The muscle that makes the Hwasa look.

exercises.name: Leg Press (wide + high)
exercises.cue: Feet wide and high on the platform, knees out — inner thigh plus glutes. Shapes the front of the leg.

exercises.name: Adductor Machine
exercises.cue: Squeeze the pads together slowly (3s in), controlled on the way back. The best inner-thigh exercise there is.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.cue: Back of the leg — the counterpart to the leg press. Pull the heels under the seat, squeeze, controlled return.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Sit down, handles at chest height, press forward, controlled return. Fixed path, nothing to set up.

exercises.name: Triceps Machine
exercises.cue: Maintenance. The machine instead of the cable rope — simpler on your own. Back of the upper arm, the 'underarm' area.

exercises.name: Ab Machine
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Fixed ab machine with a weight stack — fold under control, slow on the way back.

pull.title: Upper + Glutes
pull.focus: cable tower — alternating sets with Philipp
pull.note: Friday with Philipp at the cable tower. She's out at 13:00, he arrives ~15:30. Same station: her set, his set. Her rest is his work time.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: New for you. An emphasised shoulder makes the waist look narrower — exactly the Hwasa effect. Lead with the elbow to shoulder height.

exercises.name: Wide Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Bar to the upper chest, squeeze the lats. The back width that makes the waist look smaller.

exercises.name: Cable Row (neutral)
exercises.cue: Sit upright, pull to the belly, shoulder blades together. Posture plus the defined back look.

exercises.name: Glute Drive Machine
exercises.cue: Glutes again — twice a week is what drives growth. 3 sets here so Monday's 4-set block isn't overloaded. (Philipp does 2 maintenance sets here.)

exercises.name: Rear Delt + Face Pull
exercises.cue: New — this was missing entirely. Rear delt fly straight into a face pull. Rear shoulder, posture and shoulder health in one.

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Elbows fixed at your sides, curl up and squeeze, slow on the way down. Toned comes from control, not weight.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Kneeling, fold the ribs towards the hips, hands fixed at the ears, slow on the way back.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise (cross-body)
exercises.cue: Stand on the band with the opposite foot so it crosses the body — that keeps the tension at the bottom the way the cable does. Lead with the elbow.

exercises.name: Band Chest Press
exercises.cue: Anchor low behind you, stand away from the door, handles at chest height, press forward and upward. Feels almost identical to the cable. More tubes = more resistance.

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown (kneeling)
exercises.cue: Anchor the band at the very top of the door. Kneeling, wide grip, pull the elbows down and out towards the ribs, squeeze the lats.

exercises.name: Band Triceps Pushdown
exercises.cue: High anchor, elbows fixed at your sides, press down until straight, squeeze.

exercises.name: Band Squat (light)
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Stand on the tube, handles at the shoulders, high reps, light. Just hold.

exercises.name: Band Kneeling Crunch
exercises.cue: Anchor the band high, kneeling, fold the ribs towards the hips, hands fixed at the ears.

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
exercises.cue: Lower back flat, arms long. Build up to 40s.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise (cross-body)
exercises.cue: Second side-delt hit. Opposite foot on the band for tension at the bottom, lead with the elbow.

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown (kneeling)
exercises.cue: Anchor the band high, kneeling, wide, elbows down and out — replaces the pull-up, no bar needed.

exercises.name: Band Seated Row (low anchor)
exercises.cue: Low anchor, or looped around both feet. Sit upright, pull to the belly, shoulder blades together.

exercises.name: Band Rear Delt Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: No anchor: band in both hands in front, arms straight, pull apart to the chest, lead with the little fingers.

exercises.name: Band Face Pull (mid anchor)
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Anchor at head height, pull to the forehead, elbows high and wide, rotate externally.

exercises.name: Band RDL (bilateral)
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Carabiners into one handle, stand on the loop, hinge back with a soft knee, 3s down, squeeze the glutes.

exercises.name: Band Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Stand on the band, elbows fixed, curl up, squeeze, slow on the way down.

exercises.name: Band Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: First — glutes are the priority. Tube over the feet (under the arch), shoulders on the sofa, handles over the hips. Your bodyweight anchors the tube. Drive up, squeeze 2s at the top.

exercises.name: Band Squat (wide + high)
exercises.cue: Stand on the tube, feet wider, handles at the shoulders, 3s down. Inner thigh plus glutes.

exercises.name: Band Adductor Squeeze (lying)
exercises.cue: Band around the ankles, on your back, legs apart, squeeze together for 3s, open under control for 2s. Burns fast.

exercises.name: Band RDL (bilateral)
exercises.cue: Back of the leg. Carabiners into one handle, stand on it, soft knee, 3s hinging back, squeeze the glutes.

exercises.name: Push-Up (knee or standard)
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Knee version to regress, 3s down. Chest and triceps in one.

exercises.name: Band Triceps Pushdown
exercises.cue: Maintenance. High anchor, elbows fixed, press down until straight.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Lower back flat, opposite arm and leg, breathe out as you extend.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise (cross-body)
exercises.cue: An emphasised shoulder for the Hwasa silhouette. Opposite foot on the band, lead with the elbow.

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown (kneeling)
exercises.cue: Anchor the band high, pull the shoulder blades down — back width frames the waist.

exercises.name: Band Seated Row
exercises.cue: Around both feet or a low anchor, upright, to the belly, shoulder blades together.

exercises.name: Band Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Glutes twice a week. Tube over the hips, squeeze 2s at the top.

exercises.name: Band Rear Delt Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: Band in both hands in front, pull apart to the chest, lead with the little fingers. A defined back.

exercises.name: Band Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Maintenance. Stand on the band, elbows fixed, slow on the way down.

exercises.cue: Maintenance. Lower back flat, opposite arm and leg, breathe out as you extend.

cardioProtocol.context: Philipp's weight dropped most in July while traveling (~8,000+ steps/day). Back home: 3,000-4,000 steps, plateaued. Structural gap, not a training problem.

zone2.note: at 4 km/h lands around ~100 bpm — Zone 1, too low
zone2.appleWatchSetup: Workout → Indoor Walk → ... → Heart Rate → Range 106-124 bpm, vibrates on drift
zone2.eveningRule: after 20:00 Zone 1 only (under 100 bpm) — Zone 2 late disrupts sleep
zone2.adhdBonus: even 100 bpm rhythmic walking regulates dopamine/noradrenaline — never wasted

stepTarget.parkingHack: park on the residential street before the destination rather than the lot — about a 5 min walk each way, same spot every time, no detour. ~1800 steps round trip, ~9000/week
stepTarget.badWeather: park in the lot — no penalty rule
stepTarget.evening: pad during show/podcast, Zone 1, effortless NEAT
stepTarget.why: +3000 steps/day ≈ 200-250 kcal without compensation — bigger lever than the weight gap alone

philipp.primaryRule: start low in rep range (e.g. 12), climb over weeks to 15 across all sets, then raise load and drop back to 12. Side delt target: clean 15 → 6kg. Pulldown/row/chest: +2.5kg when all sets hit top of range. RIR 2 non-negotiable in a deficit.
philipp.maintenanceRule: 2 sets, same weight as last time, RIR 3, never progress — one number, no decision
philipp.missedSessionRule: never two in a row. One missed session is life, two is a pattern. Sunday shared session is the safety net — minimum 1x/week structurally guaranteed.
philipp.deload: every 6-8 weeks, 1 light week at ~60%. In a deficit, err earlier — cortisol is the enemy of muscle retention.

eunice.primaryRule: form before load; on glutes she can push closer to failure (RIR 1-2)
eunice.mindMuscle: squeeze and hold at the top of every rep — feeling the muscle matters more than the number
eunice.formFirst: a clean rep beats a heavy one you don't feel in the target muscle
eunice.deload: every 8 weeks, 1 light week — needed less often than Philipp since she's building, not cutting
